# Phase 1 chart audit

**Audit complete for all 105 Section B IDs.**

Every row and repair specification has been reassessed against the expanded source set and completed close pass. Raw posts and matched figures take precedence over archive write-ups. Existing implementation charts were retained where their geometry and input hashes were unchanged, then compared with the refreshed sources.

Additional source detail pass: 131/131 PDF pages; 158/158 figures inspected in their post context with native pixels and close crops. [page-by-page observations, limits and affected IDs](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/source-recheck-2026-09-11/raw_detail_pass_2026-09-11.json>).

This report audits the retained Phase 1 implementation against the supplied sources. It contains no Phase 2 work and makes no production recipe changes. Repair instructions at the bottom are specifications, not implemented fixes. Source conflicts stop faithful certification of the affected ID.

The four verdicts have different meanings: `source_ok` checks whether FORMULAS describes the source; `code_ok` checks construction and timing; `score_event_ok` checks the event and denominator; `chart_ok` checks the plotted implementation against the source geometry and sequence. `cannot-tell` preserves unpublished or ambiguous source details; `gap` and `blocked` preserve missing inputs. A retained positive is never treated as proof that the source recipe should fire.

Audit outcome: 102 IDs have at least one definite mismatch. All-four-yes IDs: R-P13. Blocked and unavailable inputs remain explicit in their individual verdicts.

Implementation plots state their own time basis, normally America/New_York. Source charts have no assumed default timezone: posting timestamps, export timestamps, displayed axes, author session names and exchange clocks are separate evidence. An export stamp alone does not prove the axis timezone. Convert only from a supported source timezone/offset on that session date, account for daylight saving, and retain an unresolved clock mapping when evidence is insufficient. EST is a fixed UTC-5 offset; it is not a year-round synonym for New York time. Bar timestamps in the implementation plots are starts; a one-minute close is known one minute later. Native contracts, cash indices and ETFs retain their own price coordinates.

User clarification on September 11: Asia, London and other reference highs AND lows remain active only while unvisited. Apply that requirement independently to both sides. A first revisit consumes the reference and ends its active line; a later revisit is not a fresh target or sweep setup. Historical range geometry may remain visible as history, and the event begun on the first visit may still develop a subsequent confirmation, but neither restores an active unvisited reference. Source descriptions and older implementations that reuse visited levels must be identified separately from this requested behavior.

Source coverage: 41 PDFs / 711 pages reread; 330 original distinct figures and 18 vector pages re-viewed, preserving the earlier crop reviews; 158 figures in the added PDFs; 85 Pine/archive/supplement files (including the one-line README); 13 prose/reference/manifest files; the separate native-product reference image; two videos with review limits recorded. The supplied Pine archive has 83 files including README, not the 84 asserted in the wiki. The supplied hourly_stats_levels and magic_hours files end mid-statement, so their visible logic is not a complete executable source. [source coverage and hashes](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/source-recheck-2026-09-11/source_coverage.json>).

The added Greenbird raw post figures supply visual evidence previously unavailable from the pack. Cached PDF figures without a matching post retain that limitation. Zip images are used only after a verified match to a PDF post; four unmatched Spain stills remain unused. Video observations preserve their sampling and audio-transcription limits. The archive gap list and older assistant proposals are secondary context, not author formulas. [new figure reviews](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/source-recheck-2026-09-11/new_figure_review.json>); [zip associations](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/source-recheck-2026-09-11/zip_caption_candidates.json>); [video reviews](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/source-recheck-2026-09-11/video_review.json>).

Dated evidence: 245 price/geometry charts plus 16 native-product supplements, each manually inspected. Every ID has at least two dated charts. These distinguish source positives, named-default positives, prerequisite-only cases, negatives and unavailable source events. A further chronological scan of 642 eligible sessions with complete RTH bars found later A07/A08/A09 sequences, an A10 no-through-open positive and true P02/P06/P19 event negatives. It found no J03 positive under the specific existing extended/single-path and 15-minute EQ-hold conditions. Missing author definitions or unbuilt source inputs remain explicit limitations; the audit does not certify their proxy-positive charts. See [additional sequence evidence](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/additional_sequence_candidates.json>).

The source label distinction is material: `pRTHVAH/VAL` is prior RTH value, while `pdVAH/VAL` is prior full ETH value. Current/developing VP, prior price extremes, range EQ, range open and RTH open are separate objects. The dated January 2 Jumbo figure places the purple Range OP at displayed 09:00 near the range finish, distinct from the forming interval’s first print; its absolute axis mapping and later source configurations must be kept explicit. The June 8 shelf rectangle is a manual profile annotation; the 302-lot bubble is a print, and neither alone constitutes a computed absorption signal.

Verification: 598 existing fixture checks passed, but several fixtures test helpers that the producer does not call, and at least one forces its pass flag. Strict replay compares the union of stored and fresh keys: 638 recipe rows lack the newer A02/A06/A18 fields, and 658 level rows lack four newer P16 bounds. All 668 failure rows match. Fresh assembly changes A02 on 371 dates, A06 on 311 and A18 on 386, out of all 668 rows (not the eligible-session denominator). Tape replay on 33 selected dates changes OFM on 22 and squeeze on 26, on 27 distinct dates. Missing s04_rev in the direct helper replay is wrapper metadata, not a demonstrated event change. The intentional S08 recipe override is also not a stale-tape disagreement. Chart headers retain the original scorer result; fresh disagreements are identified in the case notes. ## Per-ID repair specifications

Apply these only in a separately authorized implementation task. Do not create a new faithful recipe to repair a source contradiction. Keep author definitions, explicitly named research defaults, unavailable inputs and outcome measurements distinguishable. Every event record must identify its instrument/contract, session scope, source/variant, level bounds, feature cutoff, known_at, touch, confirmation, invalidation and outcome horizon. Unknown or incomplete observations are null with a reason, not false.

Common implementation requirements: identify the source display timezone, the strategy session timezone and the instrument exchange calendar separately. Use a named IANA zone with date-specific daylight-saving rules where established; a fixed UTC offset is valid only when that is the stated source convention. Preserve both raw display time and converted event time with the evidence for their mapping. If that mapping is unresolved, stop clock-dependent source certification instead of treating the chart as EST or shifting its range to fit. Then resample on the declared session clock; require complete bars; advance close-based known_at to bar completion; use an explicit tick-rounding policy; scan events chronologically; freeze chosen levels at the decision time; never select a level or direction using later extrema. Do not count one extended visit as multiple retests. If a one-minute bar contains both success and invalidation with unknown order, inspect available executions or keep the observation ambiguous. Cache identity must include source/producer version, required schema keys, input hashes, clocks, parameters and eligibility. Validate the schema before reuse; a matching revision number alone is insufficient.

For profile work, include zero-volume price bins within the price grid, define tie handling, retain aggressor-unknown volume separately and keep fixed prior profiles separate from developing profiles. Quantile/volume baselines used at an event must use only observations available then. Rates require an explicit eligible population, censoring and event unit; conditional empty populations have n=0. A presence/touch statistic must not inherit a confirmation, hold, reversal or target-reaching label.

Reference-high/low lifecycle required by the user: assign each completed reference a stable ID, side, price, formation interval and known_at. Scan all subsequent available prices from known_at, including overnight trading before a later decision window. For each side store first_revisit_at and stop the active line there. An exact visit consumes freshness independently of any separately named two-tick sweep-depth threshold. Keep missing coverage as freshness unknown; do not infer unvisited from absent bars. Preserve a first-visit sweep/failure episode through its confirmation and outcome, but do not rearm that same reference after price leaves and returns. Only a newly formed reference with its own ID can be fresh again. Keep the opposite high/low independent, and distinguish a historical completed box from its active target lines. Opening-price lines, profile value and other objects need their own sourced lifecycle; do not erase them merely by analogy to a session extreme.

### R-J01 — Judas reversal at the projection ladder

The manual shows reversal areas on both sides, overshoot and price confirmation. Its January 28, 2025 example closes below the lower 0.5 projection before rebounding, contradicting FORMULAS’ strict G invalidation. The new raw October 13, 2025 post explicitly takes both range sides before the 09:40–09:50 reversal; the first swept side is not necessarily the later reversal side. The SDRange upgrade displays configurable .33/.66 and 1.33/1.66 ladders, so the manual’s .1/.2/.3/.5 study and later configured ladders need separate source versions. Neither the raw posts nor the video publishes the reversal statistic’s joint denominator or the PZone engine. The close pass adds a June9 circled buyer failure approximately one full outer-range width above R-Hi, and May15/19/20 projections consistent with smaller inner gray spans rather than the larger shaded price box. Those later layers are not a universal extension of the manual ladder, and their blue lines are not arithmetic EQ. The4537 figure is an input-day count, not a published trade denominator.

July 10's retained positive is selected with knowledge of the deepest level reached over the full AM. A shallower early reversal and a later 0.5 touch are collapsed into one flag; the source reversal example violates the documented invalidation rule. The new July 10 source figure shows a later prior-value fail-back, outside the headline reversal window; that authored execution cannot validate this retained morning positive. Correct range bounds alone do not establish the source sequence.

| source_ok | no | FORMULAS applies a strict invalidation and first-side/deepest-ladder recipe that disagrees with the Jan28 body overshoot and Oct13 two-sided sequence; June9 and the later inner-value geometry further defeat a universal outer0.5 claim. |

**Build steps:**

1. Stop the faithful J01 claim. Retain the current G-default calculation as a named research variant until the source-compatible overshoot/confirmation definition is resolved; do not silently relax invalidation to make the historical example pass.
2. For the older manual variant only, preserve W=H69-L69, EQ=(H69+L69)/2 and H69+kW/L69-kW for k=0.1,0.2,0.3,0.5, with explicit shaded area bounds and tick policy. Version the outer price-range geometry separately from later inner-value projections and adaptive PZones. May15/19/20 inner gray spans131/81.5/49.75 points generate the displayed later projection spacing, while their blue lines are not arithmetic midpoints. Their complete value estimator is unpublished; do not replace it with outer H/L, or label it EV without evidence.

### R-J09 — London reversal model

All four October6/7/8/13 source figures begin EQ/quadrants/projections at displayed02:00, one hour before the red03:00 action marker, with a separate06:00 marker. FORMULAS/code freeze the00–03 box at action start03:00; that zero versus one-hour freeze-to-action interval is a definite mismatch independent of a uniform timezone conversion. The source axis timezone and formation start remain unpublished. Earlier18:00–19:30 prices below the drawn low exclude an18:00 start on THAT displayed axis, not every possible18:00 NewYork interpretation. Extrema-line origins do not establish the start;20:00 is only an unconfirmed source-display candidate.

All three implementation plots start levels at the00–03 NY box finish. The source instead freezes levels one displayed hour before its action marker. **Build steps:**

1. Use only levels available when the execution occurs. In the code’s NY configuration, 06–09 H/L/EQ/projections are available at09:00 and cannot be compared to02–05 London prints. This is an internal code leak independent of the author’s axis timezone. Resolve source London references/version separately, including R-J09 build start and clock; prior-session levels require explicit lifecycle rules.
2. Keep NY100 and London75 thresholds, window boundaries and NQ instrument identity explicit. A full09:30–16:00 NY version is distinct from AM-only. Compute London independently of AM trade availability. Do not copy NQ thresholds to MNQ or pool multiple contracts silently. Preserve the printed threshold wording and comparison operator: exactly100/75 inclusion needs a declared variant if the source wording does not settle equality. Do not infer the source London clock from the code02–05 window.
3. For each execution retain timestamp, price, size, aggressor side, instrument, threshold, level_id and available_at. Join to the same level’s actual touch and the named15min response window; out-of-window prints must not qualify. _big_at currently drops aggressor side and returns only a boolean; return a timestamped observation record without inventing signed direction. Level location tolerance two ticks and15-minute response are named parameters unless separately sourced.
4. Evaluate rejection/continuation and overlap with the separately defined absorption observation after the matched print. Report at-level print presence and conditional response rates separately, with touches-without-print as the comparator. Never convert aggressor sign alone into expected price direction.
5. Carry opening context, prior RTH/ETH value and developing footprint/profile snapshots at the actual interaction cutoff. Preserve manual shelves as observations; their construction is unpublished. The June8 302-lot bubble is near29358, visibly away from the drawn EQ near29343, and is separate from an earlier lower-footprint test. Do not claim an exact two-tick EQ match from a caption calling it midpoint. Later inner-value blue references need their own identity; they are not necessarily arithmetic time-box EQ.

**Build steps:**

1. Stop the faithful numerical confirmation claim. Preserve author-observed RTH volume/delta layers and the top35% highlighting statement separately from an explicitly named detector. Require the filter population, size statistic, ties, lookback and whether highlighting changes totals before asserting source equivalence; do not silently choose session-so-far aggregation.
2. At each level interaction build buy, sell, total and signed-delta bins only from executions available then. Store instrument, RTH start, available_at, tick width, aggressor coverage and unknown-side volume. Unknown volume belongs in total/quality, not invented delta. Keep the June8 earlier low footprint and later302-print candle as separate event IDs.
3. For the named EQ±2-tick /15-minute experiment, freeze a declared pre-interaction baseline and save actual local buy/sell totals, raw price path and measured adverse excursion. Replace the literal excursion2. Require nonempty valid signed trades and a supported baseline; zero medians/empty bins cannot yield positive two-sided confirmation. Record detection completion after the observation window.
4. Implement a separately named taper measurement with contiguous price ordering, declared tail extent, bin grid and cutoff. The10% tail and strictly decreasing absolute delta are experiments; a volume shelf, local signed-delta taper and one large print are separate features. Preserve aggregate and highlighted views separately.
5. Join the observation to the same frozen level area and later reject/continuation outcome, with explicit invalidation and no-observation comparison. The source’s highlighted29335–29360 area, EQ≈29343 and302 print≈29358 are different objects; no two-tick equality should be inferred. Later imbalance/isolation engine updates require a separate version.

- Source June8 earlier net-positive D1409 candle must retain negative lower-price cells; the later D−1020 candle and302 print must remain distinct. Whole-candle/session delta cannot replace local structure.

### R-J18 — Three-candle order block and rejection block

The OB is the full second candle's H/L, confirmed by C3 closing beyond C2. The rejection block is the sweep candle's wick. Source pages distinguish midpoint entry, midpoint stop and wick-extreme stop; p29's conservative-stop prose conflicts with the drawn wick-low stop.

The3m m05 OB branch has the correct full-C2 geometry, but the family omits2m/5m, other source locations, the rejection block and stop/entry variants. The source stop contradiction must be resolved without changing the OB into a wick-only box.

### R-J20 — Delayed cycle2 on10:00 release days

The source describes a later reversal after10:00 news, not simply a later first projection touch. It does not define an exact release universe. FRED returns dates, not intraday times ([API documentation](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/release_dates.html)); its sample Michigan dates match the university's final-release calendar, but the JSON omits preliminary releases such as2024-01-19 and2024-02-16 ([official dates](https://data.sca.isr.umich.edu/fetchdoc.php?docid=75443)). This is incomplete release coverage, not proof that all FRED dates are delayed updates.

### R-J21 — News, range condition and target expectations

### R-J22 — Failure signatures and three failed attempts

The source enumerates no-rejection, momentum, extended-body, timing, extended-move and volume failures, plus three failed reversal attempts at a level. Three consecutive bars touching a level are not necessarily three attempts.

Production picks±0.5 from the finalAM path, selects only the first three near-level one-minute bars and compares same-bar extrema distances with0.25W. The last bar can be forced to zero response. It does not construct distinct failed attempts or score the remaining source failure signatures.

Keep missing confirmation/volume branches gap rather than false. Window-violation labels apply only to the selected historical09:40–09:50 branch. Raw June9 buying failure and July28 continuation demonstrate opposed flow/price, without publishing one numeric momentum threshold.

### R-J24 — Post-entry excursions and management observations

The manual and raw posts describe multiple entries, partials/adds, early exits, reversals and targets as context-dependent management. Raw examples distinguish intended targets from fills, broker averages from drawings, profit-protecting stops from initial risk, and completed trades from untaken opportunities. No single fixed management or risk-distance formula is published.

The645/647 rate counts positive MFE from an assumed m05 price using extrema that can precede any touch/entry. It omits the requested multiple horizons, target chronology and valid risk denominator.

**Refreshed verdict reasons:**

| check | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| source_ok | yes | Post-entry management and target observations are sourced. The raw archive contains varied manual actions, not a universal single±0.5 entry/stop/partial formula; thisPhase1 row can only measure explicitly defined outcomes after a valid parent entry. |
| code_ok | no | The producer assumes±0.5 entry from finalAM side and uses the whole09:30–09:50 high/low, including pre-touch extrema. It has no entry timestamp and usesW69 as risk; the helper can return negative MFE/MAE. |
| score_event_ok | no | j24 reportsMFE>0 for645/647 sessions, omitting the requested horizons, event chronology and valid entry-to-invalidation denominator. It is not management success or a win rate. |
| chart_ok | no | Both plots were re-viewed. July10 contains favorable extrema before the assumed later interaction; December3 evaluates an unentered level before09:50 although its later return is near10:34. The source execution/stop/target lifecycle is absent. |

**Build steps:**

1. Require a parent setup with actual entry/confirmation timestamp, side and price. Source-conflicted or missing parent events are ineligible, not negative outcomes. A fill price is different from a drawn entry rectangle, current position average or source caption. Raw June12 tick-chart arrows can precede completion of their visible range; preserve that branch as source context rather than attaching it to a later frozen-box J01 parent.
2. For long entries compute MFE=max(0,max(high after entry through horizon)-entry) and MAE=max(0,entry-min(low after entry through horizon)); reverse the signs for shorts. Use execution order or censor same-bar unknown paths.
3. Produce separate09:50,10:00,noon horizons only when entry precedes the horizon. Record EQ touch/rejection, clean edge and1.0/1.33 reaches after entry, and edge-by09:50. A horizon before entry is not applicable.
4. Normalize only by a separately defined positive entry-to-invalidation distance. Remove the MFE>0 headline and any implied win/P&L interpretation; leave partial sizes and trade management simulation out of Phase1. A stop later moved above a long entry (June9 and January9) is profit protection, not initial risk. Pending targets below/above geometric references are distinct orders and are not fills. Do not reconcile asynchronous quoted P&L or partially obscured execution labels by inventing prices, fees or quantities.
5. Retain management snapshots as ordered observations with source chart date, export time, current quantity, visible order price/status and geometry IDs. July16’s suggested later long was not taken; May23’s mistaken full close differs from an intended target; January9’s earlier unfilled limit25846.50 is below the geometric D1High25850. Repeated screenshots are one event, and reported points are author claims until a full fill ledger exists.

**Acceptance checks:**

- July10's pre09:49 extremes cannot contribute to an entry made at the later m05 interaction.
- Dec3,2025's first later m05 return near10:34 makes09:50 management not applicable, not a negative MFE trade.
- All reported MFE/MAE values are nonnegative and reproducible from the exact post-entry slice.

Earlier lows cannot contribute to short post-entryMFE. The raw same-date target order is distinct from this assumed entry or a filled projection. |

### R-J25 — Trend-day retraces to confirmed swing midpoints

The tweet describes clean swing-mid retraces toward the January4 gap. The2-left/2-right5m fractal and trend definition are explicitly named observations, not an authored entry algorithm. FORMULAS' numeric fixture is internally wrong:105 is not100+0.5×20.

The producer scans1m data, pairs the first high and first low independently, ignores their confirmation order and back-applies the midpoint over the AM. Its hold flag is not the documented G rejection; the zero rate does not validate the observation.

**Source references:** [XF p.26 fig.1](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/source-figures/xfcmg2-p026-i1.jpeg>).

**Code to change:** [family_recipes.py::build_recipe_table](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/family_recipes.py:92>), [formulas_jumbo.py::j25_fractal_swings](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/formulas_jumbo.py:423>), [formulas_jumbo.py::j25_mid_retrace_hold](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/formulas_jumbo.py:436>), [FORMULAS.md::R-J25](</workspace/planning/phase-1-live/FORMULAS.md:126>).

**Clock evidence:** Code charts use America/New_York with date-specific DST. Source display clocks, release strategy clocks, trading-session labels and export/post timestamps remain separate; a numeric axis label alone is not an IANA mapping. Pivot confirmation is tied to actual bar-close timestamps, not source arrow placement. The Jan14 tweet is a qualitative swing-mid observation; its displayed axis does not establish the named5m model’s clock.

**Refreshed verdict reasons:**

| check | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| source_ok | yes | The source describes clean swing-mid retraces toward a named gap, without a mechanical swing algorithm.5m fractals and trend criteria are properly treated as named research definitions; the numeric105-versus110 fixture is an internal specification error to repair. |
| code_ok | no | Production applies2/2 pivots to one-minuteAM bars, picks first high and first low independently, ignores endpoint known_at and tests the fullAM. It also uses single-side path without the specified hold-through-noon condition. |
| score_event_ok | no | j25 uses any on-side close after a midpoint touch and no full-window close break, rather than the documented0.5R G rejection after confirmation. Its zero-of647 output cannot validate either the source observation or named procedure. |
| chart_ok | no | Both plots were re-viewed. January28 midpoint26250.875 and July10 midpoint29908.625 are drawn from09:30 despite future independent pivots; source chronological swing midpoints cannot exist before both endpoints confirm. |

**Build steps:**

1. Resample complete5m candles on the fixed RTH clock. A strict2-left/2-right pivot at index i becomes known at the close of i+2, not at i. The5m/2-left/2-right definition is a named observation model, not a source-authored rule. Keep its exact timeframe, alignment, missing-bar and equal-high/low policies in the variant ID.
2. Pair chronological alternating pivots into actual swings: low→next high for an up swing, high→next low for a down swing. Define handling of repeated same-side pivots explicitly; never combine independently first extrema.
3. Create midpoint=(swing_high+swing_low)/2 only when both endpoints are confirmed. Detect later touch and the named rejection/close-through sequence; retain swing width versus6–9 width as explicit separate R choices. Use a window starting only after the second endpoint’s confirming candle closes; measure any adverse close-through in the specified response interval, not the entireAM. The present helper accepts any close back on-side with no0.5R requirement and checks an unrelated full-window close-break.
4. Keep trend-so-far eligibility separate from final trend-day outcome. Correct the fixture: with midpoint100,R20 a0.5R upward close target is110;105 is a failure for that threshold. Replace all forced or disconnected pass checks with meaningful event fixtures.

**Acceptance checks:**

- No midpoint may appear on the plot before its second endpoint's confirmation time.
- Jan28,2026's independently chosen midpoint26250.88 must not be used from09:30.
- July10's both-side AM fails the final trend-only classification; a future trend label cannot alter an earlier pivot.

The session later breaks both sides, so the source-inspired trend-only observation does not qualify. The future label must not affect earlier pivot construction. |

### R-G01 — NYAM sweep and failed breakout

Raw September 8 explicitly waits for the completed 09–10 range, then a low sweep, failure/reclaim and a long toward its high; August 28 shows the high-side short mirror. September 8 range H 29686.75 comes from the 09:30 wick, not the earlier candle body, while range L is about 29455 and PDL about 29469 is a separate reclaim. However, its drawn stop 29436.75 lies ABOVE the full sweep low near 29424. FORMULAS’ universal sweep-wick stop is therefore not established by that drawing; its separate “49.75 above PDL” description is an entry-to-stop distance misread. Original stop revisions remain unavailable. The August 31 pre-10 short is another model, not permission to use an unfinished 09–10 box.

The source-dated August 28 replay places the NQ 09–10 box at H 29703.25 / L 29562.75, consistent in position and path with the approximate MNQ source bounds near 29704 / 29562. The code nevertheless accepts any beyond-edge wick, groups five observed rows, timestamps confirmation at block start and retains no stop/target episode or freshness ledger. Extended high/low lines persist after their visits. Source snapshot targets, pending limits and realized fills are not interchangeable.

### R-G04 — 09:30 manipulation and reclaim

It does not publish a complete hold duration, impulse-selection rule or expiry. Raw five-minute confirmation wording is explicit for PDL/TDO episodes; it does not independently make every 09:30 reclaim identical. April 28 and August 31 screenshots demonstrate other pre-10 trades but do not disclose this full long recipe. Source hold/target semantics remain incomplete.

The current implementation scans the AM window for a two-tick undercut then a five-minute reclaim, with equality accepted and no hold or target episode. ### R-G05 — TDO close-through after a named sweep

Raw September 9 replies explicitly correct the level to the MIDNIGHT opening price. September 3 names a close below it after an Asia-high sweep “in this case,” and September 9 shows a completed-range high sweep followed by a separate TDO crossing. A later literal TDO retest is not universal: the actual September 9 retracement peaks below TDO despite an illustrative zigzag touching it. A TDO wick alone is not the named-edge sweep, and a Pine touch statistic is another event.

The producer treats the first AM bar already beyond TDO as a wick, chooses its earliest side, and looks for an opposite close without any separate reference ID. It can miss a later genuine crossing and has no overnight association. January 28’s undercut/reclaim around 09:36–09:39 remains a retained false because the earlier already-above-TDO state selected the opposite branch. The source’s high/low reference must also have been fresh before its first sweep.

### R-G08 — Overnight prior-extreme reclaim sets bias

The pack describes overnight prior-low sweep/reclaim establishing next-AM bias; the raw archive distinguishes previous-day, previous-week and opening-range levels and shows several pre-completion overnight longs. Raw PDL wording expands to previous day’s low without publishing RTH versus full-session construction. November 19 is a PREVIOUS-WEEK low reclaim, not interchangeable with PDL. The August 11–12 long begins before Asia finishes and targets changing prior-day/TDO references; its final drawings do not publish a universal overnight PDL algorithm or hold-to-open rule.

The code uses prior RTH extrema, requires an overshoot strictly greater than two ticks, then substitutes the final 09:29 one-minute close for a causal reclaim/hold. No per-side bias event, initial freshness or later pullback outcome is stored. January 10’s prior field actually comes from January 8 in the retained session sequence, with an intervening coverage/calendar gap; its first observed 08:30 low sweep cannot certify that the prior level was globally unvisited.

### R-G09 — Stacked high sweep, bearish shift, NWOG target

The compiler’s July 27 reconstruction describes PDH, Asia high and London high sweeps, failure, bearish structure shift and NWOG destination. Raw NWOG posts support the destination sequence, and actual April 23/August 27 charts show London 02–05 with local UTC-4. ### R-G10 — Repeated fades on the pressure side

Raw August 20 explicitly says shorts only on a choppy day. Its 2-minute screenshot contains red entries and blue covers before 09:30 and inside still-forming 09–10/10–11 boxes, plus a later gray-high failure. Therefore FORMULAS’ universal two-completed-box sweep/failure recipe cannot explain all those scalps. August 27 separately claims two trade attempts; these are not automatically two fresh levels or two independent setups. Numerical pressure/bias and entry rules remain unpublished.

fade_count is only int(any-side NYAM failure)+int(any-side 10–11 failure), capped at two. July 10’s positive combines a LOW failure and a HIGH failure; that is not repeated short-side fading. The August 20 source-dated replay broadly matches both hour boxes and later gray-high reversal, but a positive two-boolean count cannot reproduce the earlier source executions, side or actual trade count. Reusing a visited box as fresh would also violate the user’s clarified lifecycle.

| check | verdict | reason |

**Build steps:**

1. Stop faithful certification at the source/FORMULAS trigger mismatch. Preserve the existing two-box-any-side count under a descriptive name; do not repair it by inventing a pressure classifier or retrospectively assigning all source arrows to completed boxes.
2. Separate reference events from trade attempts. Store the actual selected range/level ID, side, first visit, sweep/failure confirmation and any executions linked to that episode. Red entries and blue covers on a shorts-only chart are different actions, not alternating long/short signals.
3. Apply the user’s first-revisit requirement independently to BOTH reference highs and lows. Preserve ID, side, formation interval and known_at; scan all subsequent trading before any later decision window; stop the active line at first_revisit_at. Consumed references cannot be fresh targets or new first-sweep setups. A confirmation may follow the consuming visit within that same episode, but leaving and returning does not rearm the reference. Missing intervening coverage makes freshness unknown; only a newly formed reference ID resets it.
4. For a named repeated same-side failure experiment, count only eligible first-visit failures on the chosen side across independently formed references, with a pressure/bias rule known before each event. Repeated executions within one consumed episode may be counted as attempts, but never as newly fresh reference setups.
5. Retain 09–10 and 10–11 boxes with separate known_at, and include other resolved source levels only with their own provenance. No pre-completion scalp may use a finished future box. Unknown scalp trigger, initial stop or cover chronology remains unavailable.
6. Report reference-episode count, execution-attempt count, sessions with at least two same-side eligible events, and post-confirmation outcomes separately. Keep long-side experiments separately named where the source example is shorts only; both sides must obey the same freshness bookkeeping.

- August 20, 2026 replay boxes are approximately [29308.75,29470.25] and [29305,29433.50], consistent with the source’s two ranges. Earlier source scalps predate their completion; later gray-high failure cannot retrospectively certify those entries.
- A first visit ends the relevant active high/low line. Leaving and returning to the same reference does not reset freshness; another completed hour creates a distinct reference ID. Multiple broker attempts within one episode are not independent fresh setups.
- Counting three bars in one outside excursion or interpreting a blue short cover as a long entry must fail. No final day-type label may supply the earlier pressure side.

### R-G11 — A+ grade belongs to the traded setup

The pack’s grading table says a relevant range sweep plus failure, while its quoted no-sweep statement establishes a necessary condition. Raw primary posts explicitly distinguish a sweep from a failure and show full setup context; they do not publish a complete mechanical A+/B+ equivalence or numerical grading weights. September 10 explicitly says nothing screaming A+, despite longs and pullbacks, and its chart contains trades that are not all failures of the 09–10 low. Treat the compiler’s grading table as reconstruction, not proof that any day containing one failure is A+.

aplus_failback correctly pairs sweep and failure by the same dictionary key, but then ORs Asia, NYAM and the 10–11 stand-in for previous hour across the whole day. It does not grade the actual traded reference or entry time, enforce freshness, or cover all previous hours. One fixture simply sets pass=True; the reporting definition can say sweep observed even though the helper requires failure too.

### R-A01 — Balance-edge fade to the fixed POC

The balance drawings show both edge bands and rotations toward POC. Fixed prior value is an explicit research construction; the source does not publish the G-default distances or band thickness. MAMT p.5 says most excursions return, while p.9 calls the general return about one in five: that statistical claim has an internal denominator/direction conflict.

The fresh producer calls both edge rejection helpers, but discards inside-balance eligibility and POC reach. The helper evaluates acceptance over the whole AM, and its POC search starts at the window beginning and measures 60 minutes from touch rather than confirmed rejection. July 10 is a valid named fade example; that does not validate the omitted conditions on other days. A fresh January2 check returns vah_reject=1 and inside=0, directly exposing the ignored eligibility. July10 rejection is known09:33 and a later POC touch exists in the09:33 bar.

### R-A02 — Ledge break, retest and continuation

A ledge is the edge of a volume shelf. The figures show multiple fixed ledges around POC; they do not define a universal median-volume threshold. Prior VA boundaries alone are a different named level set.

### R-A03 — Re-entry, inside hold and opposite-edge traverse

The loose 80% statement conditions the traverse on re-entry and acceptance inside prior value. The 30-minute hold and 16:00 horizon are named defaults, distinct from the two-period strict rule. AMT1 also conditions the trade on order-flow confirmation; keep a price-only traverse statistic separate when tape cannot be trusted.

The current helper handles outside opens only. Its held-inside check enforces one boundary, so price can exit the far side immediately and still pass. Target timing is compared with re-entry, not hold completion, and only the first whole-window target touch is considered. The scorer divides by all eligible days instead of held re-entries.

### R-A05 — POC repeated failure versus through-and-retest

The POC tell is a sequence: repeated failed visits imply chop; an aggressive push through followed by a holding retest supports the far edge. POC is a fixed reference, and the source does not define the numeric visit reset or hold duration.

a05_poc_tell counts touching minutes rather than independent visits, infers direction from the first AM close, and accepts held-through OR retest-reject. Near/far targets use the entire window, including prices before the signal. Only the chop flag is scored.

**Source references:** [LIVE p.9](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/amt-on-live-markets.pdf>); [RTVP p.5](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/reading-the-volume-profile.pdf>).

| code_ok | no | a05_poc_tell counts touching minutes, selects direction from the first AM close and accepts held-through OR retest rejection. It can use the through bar as the retest and searches targets from the beginning of AM. |
| score_event_ok | no | Only poc_case==chop is scored. The source’s distinct signal classes and subsequent near/far outcomes are not measured conditionally from a confirmation. |

**Build steps:**

1. Start from a valid inside-open or A03 re-entry event. Fix the prior POC and entry side at that point. Define an explicit reset outside the touch band before a new visit may count; expose the reset as a named parameter. 4. Report the two signal classes and their subsequent near/far outcomes separately. Add an aggression filter only with trustworthy tape and a published or clearly named definition.

### R-A07 — Confirmed boundary break and later holding retest

The source drawings show a break followed by a separate return and continuation. IB is one named boundary family; the illustrated balance and shelf edges remain distinct. The numerical 30-minute hold and G-default are research choices. WIC’s native example uses a29730–29740 balance band with renewed downside toward29580, plus a separate29830–29840 upper boundary. TRAP also requires an intraday break/retest and renewed selling; these are not arbitrary first-hour H/L lines. RTVP’s roughly68% value convention remains separate from the named70% prior-RTH variant.

The producer covers both IB edges but passes the entire post-IB window to both break and retest checks. It can count the initial boundary contact as a later retest. June 9 passes despite no return to IB low 29365 after the outside hold completes. Next value, HTF filter and other source boundaries are omitted. A separate January 30, 2026 sequence breaks IB low 25790.75 at 11:55, completes the named hold at 12:26, retests at 12:30 and confirms the half-width rejection at 12:36, beyond the producer’s noon endpoint. The user-required freshness check changes that additional example: IBL25790.75 first revisits at10:30, well before the11:55 candidate, so the later event is historical boundary reuse and is not a fresh-level positive. A read-only search of complete retained sessions found no candidate under the specifically tested first-visit break +30-minute outside hold +half-IB rejection +30-minute no-opposite-close combination; this is not a claim that every author variant has no positives.

After invalidation, a later touch of the same ID cannot become a new fresh setup. Profile boundaries remain a separately sourced object rather than inheriting high/low expiry by analogy.
2. Find close-break and complete the named 30-minute outside hold. Slice the retest window strictly after confirmation, require approach from outside, then apply the directional rejection and inside invalidation rule to that same episode. Enforce the stated no close back inside during the30-minute retest confirmation; absence of a30-minute held inside break is a weaker test and must not substitute. Record the initial first-visit timestamp before applying any larger sweep-depth threshold.
3. Freeze an external next-value target and the available prior-session direction filter at setup time. Do not use a prior VA edge behind the entry as an automatically reached continuation target. A candidate next target that is an external high/low must also be fresh at selection. Do not synthesize a next-value input merely because a current prior-VA edge exists.
4. Measure target reach after retest confirmation until 16:00 and report it conditional on confirmed setups. Print boundary family and side separately; keep the source’s unspecified HTF-bias interpretation visible.

### R-A08 — Re-acceptance flips the balance bias

The relevant event is acceptance outside a balance followed by acceptance back inside it, then a move toward the opposite side. This differs from merely opening outside or briefly poking an edge.

Fresh code now evaluates both break sides, contrary to the stale FORMULAS description. Its inside hold still checks only the re-entered edge, and target lookup is whole-window and compared with re-entry rather than confirmation. The scorer reports reacceptance presence without the subsequent opposite-edge outcome. August 19, 2026 supplies a later valid named reacceptance: outside hold known10:19, reentry known11:44, inside hold known12:14 and opposite-edge touch in the12:18 bar. An earlier inside episode is invalidated before target.

**Source references:** [MAMT p.12 fig.1](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/source-figures/mastering-amt-vp-p012-i1.jpeg>).

**Code to change:** [formulas_jumbo.py::a08_reaccept](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/formulas_jumbo.py:638>), [family_recipes.py::build_recipe_table](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/family_recipes.py:92>), [recipe_score.py::_preds.a08](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/recipe_score.py:634>), [FORMULAS.md::R-A08](</workspace/planning/phase-1-live/FORMULAS.md:190>).

**Clock evidence:** Code axes use America/New_York with date-specific daylight saving and bar-start timestamps. Close-based known_at is the bar completion, and a30-minute hold needs continuous complete observations. Prior RTH09:30–16:00 and IB09:30–10:30 are declared strategy scopes; source schematics do not establish a blanket EST display axis. Keep instrument, source display clock and exchange calendar separate, including actual prior-session and early-close boundaries.

**Refreshed verdict reasons:**

| check | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| source_ok | yes | MAMT requires acceptance outside followed by re-acceptance inside, then bias toward the opposite boundary. Named30-minute holds measure that sequence; the statement does not equate it with merely opening outside. |
| code_ok | no | Fresh recipes call both sides, correcting the old one-side description. The helper still tests only the entry edge during inside hold and uses a first whole-window target search, with no complete causal episode ledger. |
| score_event_ok | no | reaccept presence omits the post-confirmation opposite-edge outcome and the held-break denominator. The helper’s opposite_edge_reach can also ignore held_out and compare with re-entry rather than completed acceptance. |
| chart_ok | no | Three charts were re-viewed: January2 escapes below the far boundary during the purported hold, July10 lacks the prerequisite outside hold, and August19’s later episode confirms12:14 before the12:18 target touch after an earlier invalidated attempt. |

**Build steps:**

1. Use both sides for outside-break candidates and require an actual complete 30-minute held break, even when the session opens outside. Set outside_confirmation to its completion time.
2. Search only after outside_confirmation for a close back through the same edge. Require all subsequent confirming closes to remain strictly between VAL and VAH for the full inside hold. A far-side escape is a traversal, not an inside hold. Preserve later eligible episodes after an earlier re-entry is invalidated; the source’s balance re-acceptance rule permits this profile-context reuse. This is distinct from rearming an expired session high/low.
3. Set bias at inside_confirmation and measure a new opposite-edge touch afterward. Stop at the defined outside invalidation; do not accept a target earlier than confirmation.
4. Report accepted re-entries conditional on held outside breaks and target success conditional on accepted re-entries. Update FORMULAS to describe current two-sided calls, while preserving the remaining defects.

**Acceptance checks:**

- January 2, 2026 crosses the far VA boundary too early to satisfy inside acceptance.
- July 10, 2026 short lower excursions do not establish the required held outside state.
- A later genuine re-entry after a failed first attempt must not be hidden by a first-touch-only search.
- August 19, 2026 VAL29563/VAH29662.5: outside break09:48, outside hold complete10:19; the later reentry11:43 completes inside acceptance12:14 and reaches VAH12:18. Reject the earlier attempt when its outside invalidation occurs before target; do not let it hide the later valid sequence.

August 26, 2026 demonstrates a valid named continuation after a41-minute traverse: first outside close known09:44, opposite outside close known10:25, retest10:25 and half-width rejection known10:28. ### R-A10 — Opening auction type and completed day type

Open drive concerns movement away from the opening price; test-drive and rejection-reverse require ordered tests. AMT and MAMT publish different day-type descriptions. Their qualitative boundaries need named numerical choices.

The current drive detector uses the 09:30 open but excludes the opening one-minute bar. It does not establish all four opening types or the separate MAMT day-type table. October 8 opening bar low 25074 is below open 25079.75, so the literal upward-drive condition is false despite the skip-first-minute flag.

### R-A17 — Second transition beyond a profile extreme

The source requires a return to balance beyond the low-volume region, rather than a taper ending at the profile edge. It distinguishes a gradual shelf transition from an abrupt ledge; numerical ratios are named research choices. The p13 native zigzag under a shelf box demonstrates structure, not quantitative volume-bin thresholds.

Current code takes today’s final RTH occupied-volume bins, chooses the deepest minimum, then looks for any median-sized bin on the lighter-volume side. Dropping zero bins changes adjacency, and an arbitrary lighter side is not the source balance orientation. No event-level rejection or ledge/shelf comparison is scored.

**Source references:** [MATH p.13 fig.1](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/source-figures/the-math-behind-auction-market-theory-p013-i1.jpeg>); [MATH p.15](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/the-math-behind-auction-market-theory.pdf>).

Use the actual exchange session and early-close calendar when determining previous completed profiles and coverage.

| check | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| source_ok | yes | The source requires a second return to balance beyond an LVN or structural edge and distinguishes gradual shelf taper from abrupt ledge. The native p13 diagram is schematic and supplies no numerical row classifier. |
| code_ok | no | The producer selects the deepest minimum of today’s final RTH occupied bins, discarding empty price rows, and searches whichever side has less aggregate volume. A single median-sized bin is not the declared accepted-volume run oriented away from the current balance. |

**Build steps:**

1. Freeze a prior RTH or explicitly named composite profile before the reaction window. Preserve zero-volume bins and every candidate minimum, with its price, neighbouring balance and orientation.
2. For each candidate, identify the current balance side and search beyond the candidate on the opposite side for the declared accepted-volume run. Do not substitute whichever side happens to contain less total volume; classify terminal monotone tapers separately. Publish the accepted run length. In the existing illustrative [150,160,40,30,140,155] fixture, 140 is below the stated median 145, so only 155 qualifies; do not call both final bins a two-bin accepted run.
3. Apply the named abrupt-step versus multi-bin-taper definitions to distinguish ledge and shelf, returning actual bounds. Make run length, volume ratios, ties and treatment of empty rows explicit. Specify the named 3× adjacent-volume cutoff and at-least-three-bin taper independently; source-provided ratios must not be claimed where only research defaults exist.
4. At later touches, measure directional rejection conditional on second-transition presence versus absence. Report shape presence separately from the event outcome, with known_at tied to the frozen profile.

### R-F04 — Per-candle diagonal stack and later revisit

FP8 p.5 highlights ask cells 220/410/512 while the printed diagonal bids 4120/3980/2110 do not satisfy the described 3–4× rule. FORMULAS resolves this by calling the drawing illustrative, contrary to the instruction to stop on a source/figure conflict. The conflict must remain open. ### R-F05 — At-level delta disagreement and intrabar POC flip

FP9 p.5 explicitly describes the flip as living inside a single candle. Its BEFORE/AFTER seven-row profiles show the POC moving from the sixth row to the second row within that candle. FORMULAS instead specifies adjacent candles, which is a different construction. The source sequence is location, absorption and flip; exact high/low position cutoffs are not printed. Native p5 does not publish numeric volumes or a tie-breaking policy; the lower highlighted row is the intended teaching state, not proof of a unique mathematical maximum.

The producer treats the entire AM as one candle and scores price/delta disagreement only. July 10 O29834.75/C29944.25 with delta−443 is true; January 2 falls with delta−457 and is false. Full-RTH POC is passed to the helper but does not affect the scored disagreement fields; the defect is missing candle/level/flip chronology, not a direct POC dependency of that flag.

### R-F07 — At-touch reload inference and iceberg limitation

The source differentiates size that replenishes as trades execute from quotes that disappear before trading, then waits for added participation. MBP-1 can support a limited at-touch quote/trade inference; it cannot identify hidden reserve size or off-touch depth as fact.

The retained iceberg recipe remains blocked. Existing BBO reload flags saturate and do not establish the source sequence. Available diagnostic executions on July10/January28 are insufficient to certify an iceberg, and no depth substitute was plotted.

A confirmed bar event is known at completion; a trade event is known only after every required execution/quote update.

**Build steps:**

### R-F12 — Aggressive or drifting approach to a balance band

The source judges how price arrives at an extreme and later confirms a genuine break/retest. It draws bands and names a15-minute check. In p4 the same extreme is described through different sides’ control and later defense/break language. The score compares median size of the last five AM prints with the first five. Equality1=1 makes July10 aggressive; August28 gives2→1 and false. Neither identifies arrival at an extreme or uses displacement, directional volume, five-minute bins or the15-minute confirmation.

| check | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| source_ok | cannot-tell | WIC supports assessing the approach and confirming an actual break/retest, but its aggressive-versus-slow discussion leaves the defended side and expected endpoint ambiguous. A deterministic fast=hold/slow=break mapping is not fully source-resolved; numerical five-minute rules are named choices. |
| code_ok | no | Current code compares first/last-five AM size medians. The unused arrival helper uses upward-only displacement, divides by sample count rather than actual elapsed time and uses endpoint volume difference; neither implements a side-aware approach to the drawn band. |
| score_event_ok | no | The daily median comparison is not an arrival-conditioned defense/break outcome. Equality is treated as aggressive despite no measured price speed, level, prerequisite state or 15-minute confirmation. |
| chart_ok | no | Both charts were re-viewed. July 10’s 1=1 medians produce true and August 28’s 2→1 false; no source approach-band episode or class-specific confirmed outcome is identified on either. |

**Build steps:**

1. Freeze the eligible prior-value/dealing-range band and its break/retest state. Find the first actual approach touch, with approach direction and feature cutoff before that touch. Use the drawn band identity rather than replacing every extreme with a zero-width line. Keep the directional fast/slow implication unresolved until the source side and endpoint are specified. For external highs/lows, test freshness since known_at and retire at first contact; distinguish the initiating episode from later historical retests.
2. For the named five-minute variant compute toward-level displacement in ticks/minute from complete minute closes and toward-level aggressive volume in each minute. Compare speed with causal prior-approach q75/q25; classify aggressive only when speed>=q75 and the five-bin volume slope>=0, drift when speed<=q25 or slope<0, otherwise mixed. Use timestamps: five equally spaced minute closes span four elapsed minutes. A 3.9-point displacement then equals 3.9 ticks/minute on a 0.25 grid; to measure five full minutes use endpoints five minutes apart. Declare regression versus endpoint slope, sign it toward the target, and implement the downward mirror.
3. Store the source15-minute confirmation separately with known_at at bar completion. From touch onward test rejection versus a complete break plus30-minute outside hold, preserving which side of the band is defended. A close on the starting side without an actual confirmed rejection is not automatically defended. Verify the outside hold and later retest independently of the arrival label.
4. Report outcomes conditional on class and eligible break/retest context. Remove the first/last-five median shortcut; retain missing five-minute tape coverage or unavailable prior quantiles as unknown.

**Acceptance checks:**

- July10 equal one-lot medians cannot establish an aggressive arrival.
- An identical final five-print sample at a different hour cannot change a previously classified approach.
- Rapid price approach with falling directional volume and slow approach with rising volume must remain distinguishable; neither is an automatic source signal.

### R-F13 — Prior-session trapped aggression and later break/retest

The source aligns a balance with traded structure, shows heavy buying at its upper extreme, two failures in prior AM/PM, and a later intraday break followed by a body-aggression retest. Its upper delta concentration is not the lower high-volume node; preserve signed-delta magnitude and profile position separately.

### R-R02 — Prior-close VIX band and source regime comparisons

The source names13,14,15–18 and20 cuts, expected daily percentage VIX/sqrt252, range completion and intraday VIX direction. Its30/50/95-point examples are ES illustrations, not fixed NQ ranges. Prior VIX close is a declared pre-open input choice; S&P-based VIX applied to NQ is a named cross-product context. The visible equation yields a percentage daily move. The narrative’s word range does not settle whether that becomes full width, a one-sided displacement or a two-sided band; those conversions require declared conventions.

The retained15–18 gate correctly uses the prior session’s VIX close: July10=15.84 is true andJanuary2=14.95 is false. That literal score event is valid. The full binning omits14, and implied/realized range, level response, intraday VIX direction and curve/context comparisons are not implemented by this ID.

**Source references:** [VIX4 p.3 fig.1](</workspace/implementation/reports/phase1-live/chart-audit/source-figures/vix-lesson-4-p003-i1.png>); [VIX4 p.4](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/vix-lesson-4.pdf>); [VIX4 p.5](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/vix-lesson-4.pdf>); [VIX4 p.6](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/vix-lesson-4.pdf>); [VIX4 p.7](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/vix-lesson-4.pdf>); [VIX4 p.8](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/vix-lesson-4.pdf>); [VIX4 p.9](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/vix-lesson-4.pdf>).

**Code to change:** [formulas.py::vix_preopen](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/formulas.py:76>), [formulas.py::vix_band](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/formulas.py:62>), [family_levels.py::build_level_table](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/family_levels.py:131>), [recipe_score.py::_preds.r02](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/recipe_score.py:661>), [FORMULAS.md::R-R02](</workspace/planning/phase-1-live/FORMULAS.md:972>).

Lookup is the preceding retained date rather than a general last-available vintage search. |

Daily VIX direction is known only after that close; leave the four intraday combinations unavailable without intraday VIX. Do not manufacture VX-curve/VVIX joins in the audit. ### R-R03 — Thesis lifetime and first invalidation cause

The source requires a labelled validity band with start/end and three possible death causes: structure, value shift or new information. Open-versus-prior-VA labels,30-minute holds and non-overlap of developing value are named research definitions rather than author-exact automatic thesis construction.

The caller hard-codes any_close_beyond=false, news=false and default developing_overlap=true. Directional death is therefore a wick across the prior VA edge; neutral theses survive automatically. The helper assigns death at the evaluation time or survival to16:00 instead of the first observed cause. July10 is neutral/true; January2 long/false after a fall throughVAH25634.

**Source references:** [C1 p.3](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/code-1-thesis.pdf>); [C1 p.4](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/code-1-thesis.pdf>); [C1 p.6](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/code-1-thesis.pdf>); [C3 p.7](</workspace/sources/documents/discretionary/code-3-orderflow.pdf>).

**Code to change:** [family_tape.py::_score_one](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/family_tape.py:357>), [formulas_flow.py::r_r03_thesis](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/formulas_flow.py:753>), [recipe_score.py::_preds.r03](</workspace/implementation/src/trading_research/research/phase1_live/recipe_score.py:667>).

**Clock evidence:** The named implementation starts at 09:30 America/New_York and evaluates at noon, using one-minute bars timestamped at their starts. A completed-close plus 30-minute hold is known after its actual confirmation interval, and news uses a verified release timestamp. The source’s thesis start is discretionary and need not always be 09:30.

**Refreshed verdict reasons:**

| check | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| source_ok | yes | C1 requires a labelled thesis band, start/end and invalidation by structure, value or information. Open-versus-prior-VA classification and held-close/value-overlap rules are named variants rather than a published automatic thesis algorithm. |
| code_ok | no | The caller hard-codes no close break, no news and developing overlap, leaving directional wick extrema as death and neutral automatic survival. The helper assigns noon death or future 16:00 survival without the actual earliest cause timestamp. |
| score_event_ok | no | An AM extreme Boolean is not a thesis lifetime or first-death-cause measurement; survival at noon cannot establish another four hours of survival. |
| chart_ok | no | Both charts were re-viewed. July 10 opens inside prior VA and stays mechanically neutral/alive despite excursions; January 2 starts above VAH 25634 and later falls below it, but the code does not time the named held-close invalidation. |

**Build steps:**

1. Create a thesis record at its actual start with long/short/neutral label, exact band, source/scope and chosen invalidation side. Keep a prior-VA open-label variant distinct from a directional premarket-level thesis; no later band redrawing may change the original record. Keep source user-entered thesis and automatic prior-VA variant separate. If the thesis targets an external high/low, test freshness from that reference’s known_at and end its active line at first revisit, on both sides independently; this may complete a thesis objective without itself being structural thesis death.
2. For the named structural death, find a complete close beyond the appropriate boundary and a full30-minute hold, timestamped at confirmation. Neutral bands can invalidate on either side. Wick-only crossings remain separate observations.
3. Track the developing profile only from executions/bars available at each update, testing the declared value-overlap rule. Join only verified news timestamps, preserving missing calendar coverage as unknown. End at the earliest actual qualified cause, with simultaneous-cause ties retained. Distinguish the time the invalidation begins from the later time its complete confirmation is known. Do not backdate a 30-minute hold to its first crossing. A missing news feed is unknown, not an assertion that no new information occurred.
4. Compute alive_minutes=end−start from those timestamps; survival at noon cannot imply survival to16:00. Permit a later new thesis only with a new ID/band/version. Report lifetimes and causes rather than a whole-AM extreme Boolean.

**Acceptance checks:**

- July10 neutral status must not hard-code indefinite survival; actual structure, value and news prerequisites must be evaluated or marked unknown.
- January2 downward crossing ofVAH25634 can end the named long thesis only when the chosen held-close rule confirms, not at the first wick or automatically at noon.
- An11:00 confirmed death produces90minutes from09:30, and a news event at10:00 must beat a later structural event.
- A fulfilled unvisited target, a structure death and a value shift remain different causes; neither an extended plotted VA boundary nor an already consumed prior high automatically supplies thesis validity.

The helper hard-codes no structure-close event, no news and overlapping developing value, so neutral remains alive despite later excursions. Full thesis state is not reconstructed. |

Price later crosses below that edge and remains much lower. Current code records death from an AM low, not the first complete held structural break or its actual timestamp. |

The source compares each market’s own AMT objective and which sister uses it first. The user’s SMT definition is prior high/low taken on one index and not another, across timeframes. A3/3 fractal detector and relative-return divergence are different objects.

### R-S06 — Two independent reasons at a reaction band

The source ES two-minute chart uses a marked prior rejection area plus a nearby minor HVN, with a long mirror and absorption. Prose says planned 1.5R, but native p7 short ticket is 1.00R ($500/20 ticks each side). The earlier audit statement that both tickets were 1.00R is withdrawn. Faithful target certification remains unresolved; transfer to NQ is a separate named study.

The current recipe has both directions, despite the stale short-only description. ### R-P01 — AM TBR daily-return sigma, first touch and return to 08:00 open

The source uses sample standard deviation of 20 previous completed DAILY simple percentage returns, anchored to 08:00 open, with first ±0.25σ touch. Its lower-timeframe branch scans for return starting on the touch minute; its chart fallback skips that bar. FORMULAS simultaneously says after the touch bar and from the touch bar itself. Stop unqualified certification until those branch semantics are explicit. Hardcoded hourly claims and milestones are not measured local rates. The source daily f_sigma()[1] is distinct from chart-bar sample history; changing the multiplier does not recalibrate its fixed statistics. MAE is measured from the open over the whole touch chart bar through reversion, while far-side MFE is drawn only after reversion.

The producer takes 19 log returns from at most 20 closes, starts with only five closes, and can substitute an RTH close. Both-side touch chooses smaller overshoot instead of distance from the bar open. ext_max is only the touch-bar extension. July10 returns from upper29959.91 to 08:00 open29816.75; January10 lower21232.94 touch does not return to21320.75 by noon. These validate observations of the named implemented variant, not the printed sigma distribution.

### R-P15 — Separate SSL, range-projection and OHLC-distribution envelopes

SSL, SRP and OHLC are three distinct envelope constructions; NQ Stats Price Distributions is another source with its own estimator and anchors. SSL uses100-session nearest-rank histories and has a bearish-side drawing swap plus counters mixing frozen levels with newly appended current data. SRP uses three15-minute boxes, whole-candle body extrema and range1-only statistics; its independent both-side hits are not ordered reversals. OHLC projection distribution is M+D (full range), while FORMULAS draws D alone and says latest60 despite source choosing oldest60 and unshifted live HTF data. Stop the combined faithful row. SSL direction histories are separately limited to100 per direction, observation starts at n>=2 and drawing at n>=5. SRP Both mode uses body-based true SD; OHLC doji is bearish while SSL/Price Distributions include doji as bullish. NQ Price Distributions uses fixed grids plus a different developing-daily volatility scaler; freezing at anchor does not fix its input vintage.

The producer substitutes prior60 RTH median widths, assumes MFE=.6*width and MAE=.4*width, anchors09:30 and scores only the upper threshold over full RTH. No source session quantiles, SRP ladder or OHLC history is assembled. July10 upper30071.15 is reached around15:03, outside source08–12 NY Morning; January28 upper26423.425 is unhit while the ignored lower threshold26138.55 is crossed.

### R-P20 — MVFL source delta clusters, anomaly zones and seven-vote state

MVFL source is a seven-vote hysteresis indicator using OHLC-signed sub-bar volume. RULES explicitly asks for an aggressor-delta rebuild, while FORMULAS presents the literal OHLC version; that conflict stops faithful certification. FORMULAS also clusters at close, but source bullish events use body bottom and bearish body top, weighted by absolute delta. The historical assistant upgrade proposal is not source-author proof of equivalence. C7 tests the anomaly CENTRE, not either box edge. Weighted k-means centres assign membership, but final bounds centre at (member min+member max)/2, padded to minimum0.4ATR thickness. showDeltaAreas gates cluster recalculation and therefore C4 state; ordinary sigEvent, anomaly creation and alerts continue outside plotting sessions.

The actual scorer is AM max print>=100lots AND AM price range>=8ticks:425/647. It never calls r_p20_mvfl and builds none of the source zones or seven votes. July10 max245lots/range1266ticks passes; October8 max92/range748 fails. The unused helper doubles anomaly thickness (±0.2% instead of±0.1%), and its passing fixture expects that wrong width.

Actual bounds are md±max((max−min)/2,0.4*ATR14/2), md=(min+max)/2; the weighted assignment centre is NOT the zone midpoint. Source updates only on a new event on the corresponding side and only when showDeltaAreas is true. Preserve this drawing-toggle dependency in literal mode and name any correction. Backdrawn earliest time is display origin, not availability.
4. For volume anomalies require volume>2.5*SMA20(volume), source includes current bar. Zone is close±0.001*close, full0.2% thickness. Merge centres within0.5% by retaining larger-volume event, maximum50. Keep centre, chosen event volume, created/updated times and every retired version. Merge distance is <=0.005*NEW close; scan existing centres in reverse, delete weaker neighbours and abort addition on a neighbour of greater/equal volume, retaining any earlier deletions from that loop in literal mode. For every tested L: bullish iff (C>L and previousC<=L) or (C>L and low<=L and previousLow>L); bearish iff (C<L and previousC>=L) or (C<L and high>=L and previousHigh<L). Iterate in literal stored-level order, persisting the LAST matching vote; this is not intrabar event ordering. Current cluster/anomaly updates happen before tests and current L is used against prior price fields. Unshifted HTF C1/C3/C6 can develop in real time even with default lookahead_off; distinguish a closed-HTF causal policy.
6. Preserve initial bearish bias and flip only at least4of7 votes for the other side, otherwise persist. Store all votes and their input availability at each close. Evaluate any added hold/reject or next-bar direction outcome only afterward under its own label. Fix the anomaly fixture to source width and require a producer integration test; unused helper passes cannot certify the scored MVFL family.
